The pericope context materially changes the focus into a reversal of the immediately preceding ridicule and grievance, while the legacy-unbound source is retained as a qualification.

findings.title: A returned measure reverses the nearby accusation
findings.claim: The focus turns the prior ridicule and fault-finding into a measured reversal: the practice treated as blameworthy is set beside a worse returned consequence and standing before divine judgment.
findings.mechanism: The two focus occurrences of شَرّ frame both comparison and verdict, while مَثُوبَةً makes the comparison a return of deeds; the supplied ridicule and purposeless play at 5:57:9-10 and the grievance at 5:59:5 provide the hostile scale that the paired questions turn around.
findings.reader_payoff: The question becomes an answer to a live accusation: the issue is no longer whose practice is mocked, but whose position receives the worse consequence when measured by the divine standard.
findings.containment: This is a pericope-local reversal. The packet leaves open whether the addressee is only the immediately preceding speakers or a wider hostile audience, and the focus's plain list of judgment and verdict remains intact.

epistemic.reason: The exact focus and pericope coordinates are supplied, but the reconstructed HFT source is legacy_unbound and its contextual branches are partly unresolved; the finding therefore preserves the attributed inference without presenting it as independently lexical proof.

findings.title: Worship at the center of a self-reinforcing appetite
findings.claim: The focus places worship of a transgressive authority inside a pericope-local pattern where wrongdoing accelerates, illicit gain is consumed, restraint fails, practice is deliberately produced, excess increases, and corruption results.
findings.mechanism: The focus forms at 5:60:19:2 and 5:60:20:2 establish submissive service directed to a false authority; the supplied context traces acceleration and consumption at 5:62, missing restraint and deliberate production at 5:63, and increasing excess and corruption at 5:64 as the surrounding mechanism.
findings.reader_payoff: The worship clause becomes legible as the obedience node of a social pattern that trains appetite and reproduces its own harmful conduct, rather than as an isolated cultic description.
findings.containment: The connection is limited to the supplied pericope and HFT roles. The contextual sequence may be read as a reinforcing circuit or as parallel symptoms, and the finding does not claim a wider social theory beyond this local contact.

epistemic.reason: The focus branches and every HFT coordinate are supplied, while the reconstructed legacy-unbound trace leaves six context branch records unresolved; those records are therefore retained as attributed evidence and the circuit is presented as a qualified inference.

findings.title: The comparison meets a reckoning horizon
findings.claim: The focus's recompense phrase gains a specific accounting horizon beside Fatiha's owner of the day of judgment: the comparison is a return of deeds before the authority who owns the reckoning.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier مَثُوبَةً names a return directed to the deed's owner, while the external phrase مَالِكِ يَوْمِ الدِّينِ supplies ownership of the day of accounting; their contact specifies what kind of measure the focus's worse comparison can invoke.
findings.reader_payoff: The phrase at God's presence reads as an accountable return of conduct, so the focus's comparison acquires a concrete reckoning horizon beyond a merely social judgment.
findings.containment: This overlay adds a bounded Fatiha contact to the recompense phrase. It does not replace the native pericope reversal, identify the judged people with a fixed later group, or claim an unprovided whole-text doctrine.

epistemic.reason: The focus recompense branch is independently supplied as qualified, and the external unit supplies exact surface text with lean context cues rather than full morphology; the overlay is therefore retained as a bounded contextual inference.

findings.title: The worship clause meets exclusive worship
findings.claim: The focus's completed worship of the false authority becomes a local counter-image to Fatiha's direct address, where the same act is directed exclusively toward the addressed divine referent.
findings.mechanism: The focus carrier عَبَدَ is specified by الطَّٰغُوتَ, while the external phrase إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ places its addressed object before the worship act; the shared worship relation makes the direction of submission the changed semantic detail.
findings.reader_payoff: The focus's worship clause is newly measured by destination: submission is shown as an act whose moral force changes with the authority receiving it.
findings.containment: This is a local contrast between the two supplied worship phrases. It does not claim that the focus group is identical to any Fatiha group, and it leaves the native institutional-appetite finding independent.

epistemic.reason: The focus worship branch is independently accepted and the external phrase supplies an exact worship occurrence, while the external projection is lean; the direct contrast is retained with its surface-evidence limitation visible.

branch_activations.resulting_reading: The focus names worship's misdirection as the counterpart to worship addressed exclusively to God.
branch_activations.boundary: Only the two supplied worship clauses are compared; no broader claim about all forms of obedience is made.

findings.title: The closing verdict meets the two path boundaries
findings.claim: The focus's divine anger and greater departure from the balanced way gain a concrete two-pole frame beside Fatiha's straight path, those under anger, and those astray: the closing verdict measures both displeasure and path departure.
findings.mechanism: The focus carriers غَضِبَ and أَضَلُّ عَن سَوَاءِ السَّبِيلِ contact the external terms الْمَغْضُوبِ, الضَّالِّينَ, and the straight path in 1:6-1:7; the shared anger and straying relations make the focus's final comparison a bounded path-boundary assessment.
findings.reader_payoff: The last clause becomes more precise: worse standing and greater distance are heard against the paired dangers named in the supplied prayer, rather than as an unbounded image of error.
findings.containment: The overlay does not identify the focus subjects with a fixed Fatiha category, and it does not import a whole-surah path thesis. It preserves the focus's own comparative wording and uses only the direct supplied word contacts.

epistemic.reason: Both focus branch records are independently accepted and the external ayats supply exact surface occurrences and lean path cues; the two-pole synthesis is a bounded contextual inference rather than a source-stated identity.
